whatItFakes: The paper's round-birthday and retirement briefs read only the town's full residents; a counted resident who turns 80, 90 or 100, or who retires, gets no notice.
why: A birthday notice names the person, and a counted resident has no name until the player meets them. Filling one in for the paper would make the press decide who exists.
replacement: A person a brief names is a named person, so the counted resident whose round birthday falls in the week is filled in, seeded from the world, when the notice prints (two-level population; the CTO, Nov 1, the same rule the lives lead uses), and the week's round birthdays are read from the counted population's ages by place by the same rule as a full resident.

whatItFakes: Only full readers write letters to the editor: a counted reader of the outlet never does.
why: A letter is written from a stance the reader's last story moved, and a counted reader's view is not moved by what they read (views.ts countedLean), so no counted stance cites a story to answer.
replacement: The CTO's rule (OWNER-DECISIONS Nov 1 20:00): counted readers are weighed by the same press.letter rule, times their count, from their view on the story's question and their temperament, and the writer a printed letter names is filled in, seeded, when it prints.
